_doc: Predict scoring parameters. Every tunable number lives here. The game and the simulator (sim/scoring_sim.py) both read this file, so a balance pass is a data edit, not a code edit. In every formula, p is the probability the player gave to what actually happened.

rule_notes.naive_linear: What a home-made journal usually does: win your confidence, lose your confidence. NOT proper. Included only to show why it is rejected.
rule_notes.brier_points: Core rule, Units 0-9. Quadratic (Brier) rule rescaled so 50% scores 0 and certainty scores +100. Bounded at -300.
rule_notes.log_points: Sharp mode, Units 10-12. Logarithmic rule rescaled the same way. Unbounded below, so 100% is not allowed.
rule_notes.dial_steps: The eleven confidence steps on the dial until Unit 10 (then 1% steps). A step is the probability given to the chosen side.

interval.note: Interval (Winkler) score on a log10 or linear scale chosen per question: width + miss_multiplier * distance outside the range. miss_multiplier = 2 / (1 - coverage). Lower is better.

journal.note: Journal calls earn edge points = edge_weight * (points(your forecast) - points(baseline forecast)). edge_weight 2 makes an average real call worth about one gym call (sim F: 14.5 edge points x 2 = 29 vs 33.4 for a calibrated gym call). The baseline is recorded before you commit and shown only after. A call whose baseline is outside trivial_band does not count toward gates. One scored prediction a day, written with its full chain of reasoning; extra predictions are logged unscored. OPEN: tune edge_weight on real data in Block 2.
journal.note_due: due_offset_days turns a due-date choice into a day count (Block 2: a day, not a calendar week or month, since no calendar logic exists yet). horizon_of_due buckets the four due-date choices into the three horizons the baseline table and the belts use (BL2, belts.csv): week, month, longer. OPEN: exact day counts and whether 'tomorrow' deserves its own bucket, settled with real baselines (open value 2).
journal.note_baseline: The baseline for a domain and horizon is the player's own resolved rate (yes / (yes+no), void excluded) once own_rate_min_resolved or more are resolved there; otherwise data/journal_baselines.csv; otherwise 50%.

habit.note: Flat habit points, never a multiplier on calls, so attendance can never make a bad call pay. A played day is a day with at least one call, locked prediction or resolve. It pays session_points plus streak_bonus_per_day for each streak day up to streak_bonus_cap_days, once per played day however many sessions it holds (at most 120 a day). A missed day keeps floor(streak * streak_cool_fraction) of the streak; today is never a miss while it is still going. Career points are a high-water mark of the running total of call points, journal edge points and habit points.

gates.note: A gate is a fixed exam of fresh calls, judged once at the end, never a rolling window: repeated looks at a rolling window let luck pass a miscalibrated player. Values chosen from sim/scoring_sim.py part D and G; see design/balance-report.md. Unit 1 (Block 4): judged on the exam's 200 calls only (mode exam), sealed until the last call. Failing sends the player to a repair drill on the worst band, then a new exam. A passed gate shows Rust when one of rust_triggers fires on later practice calls.

policy_notes.mild_overconfident: Stretches beliefs a little: says 82% when the truth is 75%.
policy_notes.overconfident: The typical untrained pattern: says 90% when the truth is 75%.
policy_notes.underconfident: Shrinks toward 50%: says 63% when the truth is 75%.
policy_notes.noisy: Right on average, but sloppy call to call.

gym.note: Gym session settings. Calls per session and total baseline calls come from data/units.csv (U0 and U1). The baseline is planned up front (half true, half false, spread across difficulty) and gives no feedback until the session ends; practice picks each question as you go and shifts the difficulty mix to hold the recent hit rate inside target_hit_rate. A question with no answer after timeout_seconds goes back to the pool unscored. A tap on Lock in, Next call or a summary button within tap_guard_ms of that screen appearing is ignored, so a double tap can never answer the next question or skip a reveal. OPEN: the mixes and the window are first guesses until real hit rates arrive in Block 1. Block 4: an exam sitting is exam_session_size calls drawn up front from the exam pool (questions practice never serves, so an exam call is always fresh), in exam_mix, with no feedback until the exam is judged. A question is not served again within reseen_days; of the practice calls review_share come from questions last seen review_min_days or more ago, when there are any (before day 90 there are none, so all come from the current unit's pool).

mirror.note: The calibration curve: five bands of ten points, with the number of calls under every point and a 95% Wilson error bar on every hit rate (error_bar_z 1.96). A band with fewer than thin_below calls is greyed and its bar dashed, never hidden. The bias map splits the same calls by topic (gym), domain and horizon (journal); a split under thin_below calls says 'too few' and claims nothing. Block 3.

record.note: The app nudges an Export when the last one is older than export_nudge_days and the record holds at least export_nudge_min_calls calls.

lessons._doc: The lesson engine (design/mechanics.md 4.4). Every threshold of every pattern trigger lives here; data/lesson_triggers.csv says them in words and tools/check_data.py checks the two agree on the sample size.
lessons.note: A trigger is read from the player's natural calls (modes baseline, practice and exam; a drill's forced calls never count) after the last time that trigger's flag was cleared, so old calls cannot fire it twice. L01 and L02 look at the last window calls stated inside their band, L03 at the last window calls of any kind, L04 at the last window journal predictions (rejected = the checker flagged the draft or the final wording), L15 at the last window_days days. A pattern flag needs the lesson read, then the drill, then two re-tests (the next clear_window observations after retest_after_days days from the drill) before it clears. L02's gap is 12 points, not the plan's 10: sim/trigger_sim.py found 10 fired falsely on a calibrated player 20% of the time at session-end looks; 12 brings that to 9.6% and still catches typical underconfidence 95.8% of the time in a median of 63 calls.
